extracted.intended_audience: Applicants filing PCT international applications; patent attorneys, agents, and receiving Offices processing PCT filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on procedural and substantive requirements in the PCT international phase, especially restoration of priority claims, priority-document handling, declarations in the request form, and use of earlier search results. Aimed at preparing and filing compliant international applications and related requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for requests for restoration of the right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit for complying with the requirements to request the restoration of the right of priority is two months from the date on which the priority period expired (Rule 26bis.3(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the receiving Office requires a declaration or evidence in support of the statement of reasons, it will allow the applicant a reasonable time under the circumstances to furnish such documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file a request to restore the right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The request form (Box VI) includes an option to request restoration of the right of priority; the request may also be submitted separately by letter to the receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where multiple priority claims exist, the applicant must indicate in respect of which priority claim restoration is requested. The request (or accompanying statement of reasons) may be filed subsequently within the two-month time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential requirements for a successful restoration request
rubrics_metrics.description: For the request to restore the right of priority to be successful: the international application must contain a priority claim to an earlier application and must have been filed within two months from the date the priority period expired; the request must state reasons for failure; any applicable fee must be paid; and, if required, supporting declaration/evidence must be provided (Rules 26bis.1(a), 26bis.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the priority claim was not present at filing, it must be added within two months from expiry in accordance with Rule 26bis.1(a). Fee payment must be made before expiration of the time limit (fee payment time may be extended up to two months under Rule 26bis.3(d)). If evidence is required, it should preferably accompany the request but may be furnished upon invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for restoration applied by receiving Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Two possible criteria: (1) failure occurred in spite of due care required by the circumstances having been taken; or (2) the failure was unintentional (Rule 26bis.3(a), Rule 49ter.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices must apply at least one criterion; they may apply both and let the applicant choose which criterion to seek. A finding of 'due care' is stricter but generally effective in all designated States; 'unintentionality' is less strict and may be effective only where national law permits. An RO may, on applicant request, first consider 'due care' and then 'unintentionality' if the first is not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and required information of the statement of reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement should indicate the reasons for failure to file within the priority period and contain all relevant facts and circumstances to allow the receiving Office to determine applicability of the chosen restoration criterion (Rule 26bis.3(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Offices may require a declaration or other evidence in support; any documents submitted will generally be made publicly available on PATENTSCOPE after international publication (unless exception requested/allowed). Avoid including private/confidential information not necessary to support the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision to request non-transmission of certain documents to the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can make a reasoned request that certain documents or parts thereof relating to a restoration request not be forwarded to the International Bureau (Rule 26bis.3(h-bis)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Offices may invite such requests if documents are noted to be potentially sensitive. An RO will not transmit a document/part if it finds it does not serve to inform the public and its transmission would clearly prejudice personal/economic interests and there is no prevailing public interest. Note: withholding essential information necessary to establish 'due care' may lead to national-phase review and duplication of submissions to designated/elected Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to comment on intended refusal of restoration request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the receiving Office intends to refuse a restoration request, it must notify the applicant of its intention and provide an opportunity to make observations within a reasonable time limit (Rule 26bis.3(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notification (Form PCT/RO/158) may be sent together with an invitation to file a declaration or other evidence. The applicant should use that opportunity to submit observations or additional supporting material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of a receiving Office decision on designated Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision by a receiving Office to restore a priority right on the basis of 'due care' will generally be effective in all designated Offices unless a designated Office filed an incompatibility notification; a decision based on 'unintentionality' is effective only in designated States whose laws permit restoration on that criterion (Rule 49ter.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A receiving Office's refusal can be reviewed by designated Offices. A positive decision may be reviewed by a designated Office only if it reasonably doubts that substantive requirements for restoration were complied with; purely formal grounds (e.g., non-payment of an international-phase fee) are not grounds for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: When and to whom the priority document must be furnished
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified copy of the earlier application must be submitted before the expiration of 16 months from the priority date either to the International Bureau or to the receiving Office (Rule 17.1, Rule 17.2(a), Section 411).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a certified copy reaches the IB after 16 months but before international publication, it will be treated as received on the last day of the 16‑month period. If the authority that filed the earlier application is the same as the receiving Office, the applicant may request that authority to prepare and transmit the certified copy (fee usually payable at the time of request). The applicant may instead ask the IB to obtain the priority document from a digital library (no fee) by marking the relevant box in Box VI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of priority documents via DAS and applicant steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The only available digital library in the PCT system is DAS; an earlier application is available via DAS only if the applicant has taken the specific steps to make it available (paragraph 5.070A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural steps and participating offices are listed on the DAS website. After making the application available, the applicant receives an access code and should mark the appropriate check-box(es) in Box No. VI and indicate the access code(s) or submit a written request containing this information to the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for making an earlier international application available via DAS
rubrics_metrics.description: If the earlier application to be made available via DAS is an international application, the applicant may request the receiving Office that holds it to make it available via DAS and authorize an Office of second filing to retrieve it (paragraph 5.070C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check participating Office lists to confirm whether a receiving Office will make international applications available to DAS in addition to national applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for designated Offices if priority document furnished or requested
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has furnished a certified copy or requested transmission/obtainment and paid necessary fees, no designated Office may ask the applicant to furnish a certified copy; otherwise a designated Office may disregard the priority claim after giving the applicant a reasonable time to furnish the document (paragraph 5.070D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should pay attention to fees and marking of check-boxes to avoid designated Offices later requesting duplicates. Applicants are still obliged to furnish a simple (not certified) copy to designated Offices where required (see National Phase guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and indication of International Searching Authority (ISA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more ISAs are competent to carry out the international search, the applicant must indicate the chosen Authority in Box No. VII (Rule 4.1(b)(iv), Rule 4.14bis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details on competent ISAs and their competencies are given in Annex C and paragraph 7.002.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting the ISA to take into account results of an earlier search
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request the ISA, in carrying out the international search, to take into account results of an earlier international, international-type or national search if the applicant complies with Rule 12bis.1 (Rules 4.12, 41.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the earlier search was carried out by the same Office acting as the ISA, the ISA must, to the extent possible, take it into account (Rule 41.1(i)). If the earlier search was by another Authority, the ISA may choose whether to take it into account (Rule 41.1(ii)). The Continuation of Box No. VII (item 1) contains a checkbox option and space to identify the earlier application (date, number, country).

rubrics_metrics.name: When the applicant need not furnish a copy of earlier search results
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant need not furnish a copy of earlier search results if: (a) the earlier search was carried out by the same Authority or Office that will act as ISA; (b) the earlier search was carried out by the same Office as the receiving Office and the applicant asked the receiving Office to transmit results; or (c) a copy of the earlier search results is available to the Office/Authority in an acceptable form (Rule 12bis.1(c),(b),(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If asking the receiving Office to transmit earlier search results, this may be subject to payment of a fee. If multiple earlier searches are to be considered, the Continuation sheet should be duplicated as needed and the required information provided for each earlier search.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA may request additional documents in connection with an earlier search
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA may invite the applicant to furnish a copy of the earlier application, translations (if required), a translation of the earlier search results, and/or copies of any documents cited in the earlier search results (Rules 4.12, 12bis.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the ISA may not require these documents if: (a) the earlier search was by the same Authority that will act as ISA; (b) the applicant marked the checkbox stating the international application is the same or substantially the same as the earlier application (except for language); or (c) copies/translations are available to the ISA in an acceptable form and the applicant indicated this by marking the checkbox.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office transmission of earlier search and classification results even without applicant request
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application claims priority of an earlier application and the earlier application was filed with the same national/regional Office which carried out the earlier search, the receiving Office is required to transmit a copy of the earlier search and classification results to the ISA (Rule 23bis.2(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receiving Office is only obliged to transmit earlier search/classification results that are available to it at the time of filing the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offices that may not transmit earlier search results without applicant authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Offices have notified the International Bureau that transmitting copies of earlier search and classification results without the applicant's authorization is incompatible with national law (Rule 23bis.2(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of concerned receiving Offices includes: Australia, Finland (PRH), Hungary (HIPO), Czechia (Industrial Property Office), Singapore, Israel, Japan (JPO), Norway, Sweden (PRV), and the United States (USPTO). An applicant may authorize transmission by marking the relevant checkbox in Continuation of Box No. VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant may request receiving Office not to transmit earlier search results
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Offices permit an applicant to request that the receiving Office not transmit earlier search results to the ISA (Rule 23bis.2(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receiving Offices that allow this include the Finnish PRH, the German Patent and Trade Mark Office, and the Swedish PRV; the request is made by marking the check-box in item 2.2 of Continuation of Box No. VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: When the ISA will take earlier search results into account without an applicant request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the earlier search was carried out by the same Office that acts as ISA, the ISA is required to take those results into account. The ISA may also take account where the receiving Office has transmitted earlier search/classification results or where such copies are otherwise available to it (Rule 41.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability from digital libraries or transmission by the receiving Office enables the ISA to consider earlier results even absent a specific applicant request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations that may be included in Box No. VIII (i)–(v)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of national law in one or more designated States, the applicant may include the following declarations under Rule 4.17 in Boxes VIII(i) to (v): (i) declaration as to identity of the inventor; (ii) declaration as to the applicant’s entitlement, as at the international filing date, to apply for and be granted a patent; (iii) declaration as to the applicant’s entitlement, as at the international filing date, to claim priority of the earlier application; (iv) declaration of inventorship (only for purposes of designation of the United States); (v) declaration as to non-prejudicial disclosures or exceptions to lack of novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the only declarations permitted in Boxes VIII(i)–(v). If included, the relevant standardized wording must be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and effect of declarations under Rule 4.17
rubrics_metrics.description: Declarations under Rule 4.17 enable applicants to comply with some national requirements of designated Offices already during the international phase, potentially avoiding the need to submit documents/evidence on those matters during the national phase (Rule 4.17, Rule 51bis.1, Rule 51bis.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting a declaration (e.g., under Rule 4.17(ii)) generally means the applicant will not need to submit further documents on that subject to designated Offices that require such information, unless a designated Office reasonably doubts the veracity of the declaration. The PCT does not require declarations but standardized wording must be used; otherwise designated Offices may require new declarations or further evidence later.

rubrics_metrics.name: How declarations must be presented and standardized wording requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each declaration should be made on the appropriate Box No. VIII sheet; continuation sheets must be used if needed. Declarations must be worded using the standardized wording provided in Sections 211–215 (Rule 4.17, Section 211–215).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for the U.S. inventorship declaration, applicants should choose the items/elements of the standardized wording that apply and place them in appropriate order considering case facts/chronology. Detailed guidance is in the Notes to the request form. If no declaration is made, do not include the optional declaration sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for the declaration of inventorship for the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. inventorship declaration text is pre-printed in Box No. VIII(iv) and must be used exactly as set out (Section 214); no parts may be omitted or reordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When furnished after the international filing date, the PCT application number must be added. When several inventors exist, all inventors must sign and date a complete declaration containing all inventors (even if they sign different copies), and name, residence and address must be included for each inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the declaration of inventorship for purposes of designation of the United States must be signed and dated by all inventors (Rule 4.17(iv), Section 214).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No other declaration under Rule 4.17 must be signed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of Rule 4.17 declarations by designated Offices and possible further evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated Offices that have special national requirements allowed under the PCT accept declarations made under Rule 4.17. For declarations under Rule 4.17(i)–(iv) a designated Office may not require documents/evidence on that subject unless it reasonably doubts veracity; for Rule 4.17(v) (non-prejudicial disclosures) the designated Office may require further evidence (Rule 51bis.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A declaration does not by itself establish the matters declared; substantive determinations remain with designated Offices under applicable national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: How declarations are communicated to designated Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: All declarations will be part of the published international application and will not be communicated separately to designated Offices (Rules 48.2(a)(x), 48.2(b)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices access declarations via the published application; applicants should ensure declarations conform to standardized wording if they wish them to serve nationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the check-boxes in Box No. VIII
rubrics_metrics.description: The check-boxes in Box No. VIII should be completed to allow the receiving Office to verify that the declaration(s) in Boxes VIII(i)–(v) correspond to those made in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no declaration is made at filing or declarations are not available, do not include optional sheets and do not mark the check-boxes in Box No. VIII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction or addition of declarations during the international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration referred to in Rule 4.17 may be corrected or a new (missing) declaration added by a notice submitted to the International Bureau (Rule 26ter.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A declaration may not be withdrawn once filed. For details on correction/addition procedures see paragraphs 6.045–6.050.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Box No. IX (Check List)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. IX should be completed to allow the receiving Office to verify the completeness of the documents constituting and/or accompanying the international application (Rule 3.3, Section 313).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist helps the RO verify that the international application as filed contains the number of sheets in paper form indicated in the relevant items.
